chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sulaym al-Farra', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the fasting person who applies kohl (eye medicine). He said, 'There is no harm with it; it is not food nor drink.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm with it (it is permissible)

ai.seo_question: Does applying kohl break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the permissibility of using kohl while fasting is established by distinguishing it from food and drink, as it does not reach the stomach in the manner of nourishment. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for validating medical treatments that do not involve ingestion, reflecting the principle that breaking the fast requires the consumption of substantial matter. The hadith underscores the practical ease Islam affords to believers, ensuring that necessary health measures do not invalidate the spiritual act of fasting.
